_schema.purpose: The one cross-driver CLI parity fixture for the local clone family surface (operator ruling 1 of 2026-09-06, LCM1.0c follow-up 3). Both drivers -- gwz-cli and gwz-py -- read THIS file and assert against it; neither restates these cases inline and neither keeps a copy. Add a case here, not in a driver's test module. A row pins the command line a person types, the protocol message it must build and the field values that message must carry; nothing here reaches core, the assertion is on the encoded request (or on the refusal that precedes any request).
_schema.authority: gwz-dev dev-docs/GwzLocalCloneDesign.md revision 10 section 7 (CLI -> live message) and section 11 items 11-15, plus the operator's cross-driver rulings of 2026-09-06 recorded in GwzLocalClone-LCM1.0c-Checkpoint.md section 12: (1) this file is the single source; (2) machine output spells enum values in snake_case; (3) LocalFamilyResponse.root_path; (4) `push --remote` encodes the token once, in PushRequest.remote, and an empty `--name` refuses at the driver. Where the two drivers' former copies disagreed, the design section 7 table decided. (5) The operator ruling of 2026-09-06 on the command surface (design revision 15, section 4, section 7 and section 11 item 28): local-clone creation is `gwz local clone <name> [dest] [--clean | --bare] [-b <branch>] [--from <name|path>]`, a subcommand of the family's own verb with the member name positional like `dispose <name>`; `gwz clone --local` was REMOVED without an alias, because nothing had been released or pushed and an alias born that day would be documented forever. The wire did not move: CloneLocalWorkspaceRequest, ActionKind 27, copy_source (tag 6) and every field are unchanged, so every `message` and every `fields` value below is byte-identical to the row that pinned the old spelling -- only the argv moved. Exchange stayed where it was: `merge --remote`, `pull --head --remote` and `push --remote` are not local subcommands.

_schema.provenance: Merged 2026-09-06 from gwz-py src/tests/fixtures/cli_parity/parser_cases.json (30 message cases, 15 refusals; its `accept`/`parse_reject`/`semantic_reject`/`rust_accept`/`rust_version` argv lists are that driver's general parser fixture and stay there) and gwz-cli tests/fixtures/cli_parity/local_family_cases.json (24 accept, 17 reject). Ids are gwz-py's where a row existed there; rows only gwz-cli carried got new ids. Folded: gwz-cli's `--force wat` row into local-dispose-force-unknown-name (same case, one token); gwz-py's python-only push-remote-python-clears-the-policy-binding into push-remote-family-hub, now both drivers, per ruling 4. Values that changed for a driver: gwz-cli's two push rows (policy_remote "hub"/"origin" -> meta.policy.remote null, ruling 4 and design section 7, which names only PushRequest.remote); clone-local-empty-name is no longer python-only (ruling 4).
_schema.stability: Keys and case ids are stable. Append cases; do not renumber, rename or reorder existing ones. A case a driver cannot express is scoped with `drivers`, never deleted. A case the surface itself can no longer express is scoped `"drivers": []` with a note saying why, so its id and its history stay readable.

message_cases.what: One entry per design section 7 'CLI -> live message' row, plus the section 4 `--from` selector rows and the dry-run pass-throughs. Each pins the command line a person types, the protocol message it must build, and the field values that message must carry.
message_cases.design_row: the design table cell this case pins, verbatim, or the design clause it comes from
message_cases.argv: argv without the program name and without shell quoting, byte-identical to the design's command line
message_cases.message: the generated request message's type name
message_cases.fields: dotted paths from the request root to the expected value. A path resolves through an absent (null) intermediate to null, so `meta.policy.remote` is null when the request carries no policy object at all (gwz-cli's former `policy_remote` key is exactly `meta.policy.remote`). Enum values are the protocol enum's own name in snake_case (`verbatim`, `ff_only`, `start`); everything else is literal JSON.
message_cases.drivers: optional; which drivers accept this spelling. Default is both: ["python", "rust"].
message_cases.core_refuses: optional; the GwzErrorCode core answers for this request. The CLI still encodes and sends it -- the key records that the refusal is core's, not the CLI's.

message_refusals.what: Command lines a driver must refuse before encoding any request. `refused_by` says whose refusal it is.
message_refusals.refused_by: `cli` -- the driver refuses before any core call: a typed usage refusal from the driver's own validation, or the argument parser's own rejection (an unknown flag, a missing or surplus operand), which both drivers' harnesses read the message of since the 2026-09-06 surface ruling
message_refusals.message_contains: substrings BOTH drivers' refusal messages contain. Every listed substring must appear; the wording around them differs per driver, so keep these short. May be empty when the two drivers share no wording, in which case `driver_message_contains` carries each driver's own needle.
message_refusals.driver_message_contains: optional; {"rust": [...], "python": [...]} -- extra substrings one driver's message must contain, on top of `message_contains` (gwz-cli's former `rust_needle` lives here).

message_cases.design_row: gwz local clone A ../gwz-dev-A
gwz local clone A ../gwz-dev-A (--verbatim is the default, spelled out)
Dest defaults to ../<root-dirname>-<Name> (design section 4, section 11 item 3)
message_cases.note: An absent dest is core's default, not a CLI-side path join.

message_cases.design_row: gwz local clone C dest --clean -b lane/x
gwz local clone hub dest --bare
-b is accepted with --bare as well as --clean (design section 4.3)
message_cases.note: The flags may precede the positionals as well as follow them (both parsers interleave); the design's own command lines put them after, as the section 4 usage does.

message_cases.design_row: Copy source is cwd (or --from <name|path>) (design section 4; wire field copy_source, section 7 and section 11 item 11)
message_cases.note: `from` is a keyword in both generated languages, so the wire field is copy_source (tag 6). The CLI does not decide whether the token is a family name or a path -- core resolves it.

message_cases.design_row: --from <name|path>: the path form, dest defaulting in core
--from <name|path>: the path form with an explicit dest (section 7 copy_source, tag 6, section 11 item 11)
v0 local create refuses an unsupported dry-run in core (design section 6.2)
message_cases.note: The local-family verbs pass --dry-run through for core to refuse; only the URL clone keeps its own CLI-side refusal (see message_refusals/url-clone-dry-run).

message_cases.design_row: gwz local list
gwz local dispose C
gwz local dispose C --keep
gwz local dispose C --force unpreserved-history
gwz local dispose C --force open-merge,dirty,unpreserved-history
hazard list splitting (design section 11 item 15)
message_cases.note: The split is on ',' and nothing else: no trimming, no case folding, no normalization. A deletion waiver is the operator's authorization token; rewriting it before encoding would make the CLI answer for a vocabulary that belongs to core. Core refuses ' open-merge' as an unknown hazard, which is the correct answer to what was actually typed.

message_cases.design_row: core rejects unknown hazards (design section 7): the hazard vocabulary is core's, so an unknown name travels
message_cases.note: The CLI refuses only the shapes that would be misread on the wire -- a force naming nothing, or an empty element. gwz-cli's former `--force wat` row is this case with another token.

message_cases.design_row: gwz local disband
the family verbs pass --dry-run through for core to refuse
gwz pull --head --remote A
message_cases.note: pull binds the name through OperationPolicy.remote, not a request field (design section 7: PullHeadRequest.meta.policy.remote). Core resolves a ready family name first and falls back to a git remote.

message_cases.design_row: gwz pull --head --remote origin
message_cases.note: Identical encoding to the family row: `origin` is reserved as a family name, so this reaches the git remote and never UnknownLocal.

message_cases.design_row: gwz --sync ff-only pull --head --remote root
gwz merge feature/x
gwz merge --remote A
message_cases.note: For merge, --remote is family-only: a MergeRequest field, never OperationPolicy.remote. HEAD per paired member.

message_cases.design_row: gwz merge --remote C lane/agent-17
gwz merge --remote origin -> UnknownLocal (family-only; reserved / not a member)
message_cases.note: merge --remote has no git-remote fallback, so the CLI encodes the name unchanged and core answers unknown_local (62) with the state detail in the message. Pull and push keep missing_remote for their neither case.

message_cases.design_row: gwz merge A -> git ref `A`, not a family name
an invalid or unsupported family start refuses in core (design section 6.2)
message_cases.note: merge --dry-run is a supported merge shape; the family selector does not add a CLI-side refusal to it.

message_cases.design_row: gwz push --remote hub -> PushRequest remote=hub (family); current branch to the same branch in hub
message_cases.note: Ruling 4 (2026-09-06): the token is encoded ONCE, in PushRequest.remote -- design section 7 names only that field for push -- and OperationPolicy.remote stays absent. Core reads the request field first and still accepts a policy-only token from an older caller, so this decides the bytes a driver sends, not what core will bind. A ready family row wins in core; an absent row falls back to a git remote. This row was the unresolved divergence (gwz-cli also set the policy field; gwz-py cleared it): gwz-py's encoding stands.

message_cases.design_row: gwz push --remote origin -> PushRequest remote=origin (git)
gwz local clone <name> [dest]: the first operand is the name, the second the destination (section 4; operator ruling 2026-09-06)
message_cases.note: Under the old spelling this argv shape (`clone --local dest`) was the refusal clone-local-dest-without-name. With the name positional a lone operand IS the name and the destination defaults in core; a destination is always the second operand. A path typed in the name's place is caught by core's name rules (no `/` or `:`), not by the driver.

message_refusals.note: The name is a required positional, the shape `dispose <name>` already has (operator ruling 2026-09-06), so this is each parser's own required-argument error: Clap names `<name>`, argparse names `name`. Formerly `clone --local` without `--name`, a driver refusal.

Not expressible since the 2026-09-06 ruling: with the name positional, a lone operand is the name, never a destination without one -- the same argv shape is now the message case local-clone-single-operand-is-the-name. Kept, scoped to no driver, so the id and its history stay readable.

Ruling 4 (2026-09-06): both drivers refuse an empty name before encoding, typed, with the same words. Core's own shape check (validate_clone_local) refuses the empty name and the reserved names too, so the driver's refusal is the earlier answer, not the only one; the CLI answers for the shape that would otherwise cost a workspace discovery and a family read to learn the same thing. Formerly python-only; formerly `--name ""`.

`local clone` takes a name and one optional destination; a third operand is each parser's own surplus-argument error. Formerly `clone --local --name A url dest`, a driver refusal (`not a workspace URL` / `one destination path`).
An empty copy_source is not `the cwd workspace`: the absent field means that. Encoding an empty string would ask core to resolve a nameless source.

`clone` declares none of the local flags any more (operator ruling 2026-09-06): --name, --verbatim, --clean, --bare, -b and --from are each an unknown argument to the parser, named in its own error. Formerly `is accepted only with --local`, a driver refusal.
An unknown argument to the URL clone's parser (operator ruling 2026-09-06).
An unknown argument to the URL clone's parser (operator ruling 2026-09-06).
The URL clone keeps its own pre-existing CLI-side --dry-run refusal. The local-family verbs do not copy it: they pass --dry-run through for core to refuse (see the *-dry-run message_cases).
An empty force_hazards list is `no force`, so encoding one for a --force invocation would invert the operator's authorization (design section 8.4).

The global --force before the verb is the same refusal. Design section 11 item 15: the Rust CLI cannot add a subcommand --force beside the global one, so it parses the hazard list as operands of the global flag; every command line in sections 5 and 8 stays byte-identical.

gwz-cli distinguishes an empty list from an empty element and says `must not contain an empty hazard name`; gwz-py cannot -- argparse gives a bare --force and --force "" the same value -- so it answers both with one message. Same refusal, different wording, hence the short shared needle.

Hazard names without --force never become a waiver. gwz-cli's typed refusal names --force; gwz-py's argparse rejects the extra operand as unrecognized before any handler runs. Both drivers refuse before encoding, and since the 2026-09-06 surface ruling both harnesses read the parser's message too, so the row is no longer scoped to rust.

Refused at the CLI in both drivers, although design section 7 also assigns it to core (`core rejects unknown hazards and keep+force`). Detaching and waiving loss are opposite intents; the CLI refuses the contradiction before it costs a family lock, and core keeps its own check for non-CLI callers.
local_source_name is start-only (design section 7); --continue, --abort, --status and --gc each refuse the same way.

The old create spelling, verbatim from design revision 14 section 7, is rejected by both parsers naming `--local` (operator ruling 2026-09-06). It is not an alias, hidden or otherwise, and it must not parse as a URL clone of `A` into `../gwz-dev-A`: the harnesses fail this row if any request is built.
The old clean-with-branch spelling (design revision 14 section 7), rejected the same way.
